subject: Postcall: Redwood integration recap & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 17:10:00 +0000
Subject: Postcall: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Hi Alex (and team),

Thanks again for the call today - really appreciate you walking through Acme's current search/assist flow. Quick recap to make sure we're aligned and to capture next steps:

High-level pain points you called out:
- End-user latency spikes during peak traffic (affects both chat and document search).
- Need deterministic, structured outputs for downstream business logic (we heard examples: order extraction, policy routing).
- Relevance issues on internal search - you want semantic embeddings + reranking to improve recall/precision.
- Concern about SDK integration friction: function-calling and streaming need to work with your existing microservice patterns.

What we think product-fit looks like:
- Streaming for low-latency user-facing responses + function-calling to produce structured JSON that your services can ingest.
- Embeddings + reranking pipeline: Redwood embeddings for indexing, then a lightweight reranker at query time.
- Dev ergonomics: small SDK change to enable function-calling hooks and streaming handlers; no major infra changes for the initial POC.

Suggested next steps & owners:
1) 2-week technical POC (hosted Redwood API) to validate streaming + function-calling + embeddings/rerank (Owner: Dev Patel)
2) Engineering sync next week to align on sample payloads, expected throughput, and p95 SLO (Owner: Marissa to schedule)
3) Security/compliance: we'll share SOC2 + data handling notes; you flagged need for audit logs and data retention controls (Owner: Rishi)
4) Draft SOW + estimate (attached) for Dedicated environment evaluation if POC meets criteria (Owner: Marissa)

Attachments: redwood-poc-outline.pdf (outline + minimal success criteria).

Questions for you before we kick off POC:
- Can you confirm target p95 latency we should optimize for on the POC? (You mentioned ~200ms as a ballpark.)
- Expected concurrent users/requests during peak day (helps sizing and batching configs).
- Are there any internal routing/firewall requirements for the hosted POC?

Thanks - I can send calendar invites for the eng sync once you confirm availability.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme.com>
Date: Sat, 27 Mar 2027 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Postcall: Redwood integration recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa - good summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- p95 target: yes, aiming for <= 200ms for short chat queries; for longer document search flows p95 of 350ms is acceptable as long as the UI shows progress.
- Throughput: our average is ~6k requests/day now, but with expected growth to ~20k/day by Q4; peak concurrency estimated at ~180 reqs/min.
- We definitely want to test embeddings + rerank in the POC - our current TF-IDF approach is failing on recall for new documents.
- Procurement timeline: we want to finalize a vendor decision by end of Q2; procurement will need an initial pricing range to evaluate ROI.
- Security: please share SOC2 + evidence for audit logs. Also, we may request a short questionnaire from our InfoSec team.

Cc'ing Maya (our product lead) - she will join the engineering sync.

On the SOW/hosting: we'd prefer to validate the hosted flow first, then evaluate Dedicated if the POC shows clear unit-cost or compliance benefits.

Thanks - available for the eng sync Tue/Wed next week afternoons PT.

- Alex
Alex Johnson
Principal Product Manager | Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com | +1 (212) 555-4141

4) I'll pull together a high-level pricing range for procurement to review (target: send by Thu).
